analysis.investment_thesis: CP PLUS holds genuine brand leadership in India's fast-growing security surveillance market, but at 105x P/E and with virtually zero free cash flow in FY25, the price demands perfection in a commoditized hardware business. The reported net profit of ₹351 Cr is an illusion — ₹259 Cr came from "Other Income," not operations, making the true earnings quality deeply suspect.
key_strengths: CP PLUS brand dominance in India's surveillance market with 20.2% revenue CAGR and improving operating margins (EBITDA from ₹62 Cr to ₹258 Cr over 5 years)
Near-zero leverage — D/E of 0.08 after borrowings collapsed from ₹436 Cr to ₹128 Cr in FY25
76.91% promoter holding signals strong owner-operator alignment and stable governance
key_risks: 105x P/E on 11.2% operating margins with thin FCF — a surveillance hardware company is not a software business; any multiple compression destroys value
FY25 operating CF was just ₹27 Cr against ₹351 Cr net profit — cash conversion is broken; FCF essentially ₹1 Cr
Chinese giants (Hikvision, Dahua — which CP PLUS itself distributes) compete directly and can structurally compress margins via pricing
red_flags: FY25 net profit of ₹351 Cr includes ₹259 Cr in 'Other Income' vs. -₹12 Cr prior year — the core business earned far less than headline numbers suggest
Equity surged from ₹424 Cr to ₹1,587 Cr in one year — consistent with a large equity raise that dilutes per-share value and inflates the balance sheet
FCF negative in FY24 (-₹187 Cr) and effectively zero in FY25 (₹1 Cr) despite rising reported profits — earnings do not convert to cash
EV/EBITDA of 68.76x is extreme for a capital-light-claimed business with only 11% operating margins
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CP PLUS is a real business — India's leading security and surveillance brand with a recognizable name, distribution depth, and a growing move into AI-IoT services (OnVigil). Revenue has compounded at 20% over five years and operating income at 34%, reflecting genuine operating leverage. The balance sheet is now conservatively leveraged at D/E 0.08. I can see the kernel of a good business here, and India's surveillance build-out is a genuine secular tailwind. But I need to understand what I'm actually buying, and the FY25 numbers don't hold up to scrutiny.

The reported net profit of ₹351 Cr is misleading. Operating income was ₹248 Cr, yet "Other Income" alone was ₹259 Cr — compared to -₹12 Cr the prior year. That means the core business earned roughly ₹90-100 Cr after finance costs and taxes, consistent with prior years. Yet the market is pricing the stock on ₹351 Cr as if it is recurring. Operating cash flow was only ₹27 Cr in FY25 — confirming the ₹259 Cr "Other Income" is non-cash or one-time. When I pay 105x reported P/E and 69x EV/EBITDA for what is fundamentally a 11% margin hardware assembler competing against Hikvision and Dahua, I'm not buying a wonderful business at a fair price — I'm buying a fair business at a wonderful price for the seller. At Berkshire, we pass.
